correctness.rationale: For any 2-cycle x,y the local strict-majority rule follows from one-neighbor count h_u+h_v−2x_e and threshold (d_u+d_v−2)/2. For each flip delta_e(Delta_u+Delta_v)<=0 while the sum equals sum_v Delta_v^2>=0; hence every incidence change vanishes. Boundary edges therefore complement and form a half-factor, P_h forced one and N_h forced zero; reversing this construction proves sufficiency and coefficient counting without duplication. Independent exhaustive Python checks covered all 154 parity-eligible simple base graphs on up to five vertices, 4909 binary states; all matched. The P3 unequal-parity counterexample and bridge exclusion were checked. Infinite family conclusion follows the incidence identity, not finite enumeration.
